x_failures: Minor stretch: the closing line reads Corda p.51's 'visionary darkness of the Middle Ages' (where he says no writer dealt with plant systematics) as an 'esoteric role of fungi'.
y_failures: Says Theophrastus found fungi 'lack roots, stems, leaves, flowers, or seeds', citing pp.315/94, which don't say this; cites the Erya's jun/zhi definitions to Parallel Characters pp.100/123, where the Erya appears only for 'stone rue'; calls Sterbeeck the 'first standalone printed book entirely devoted to mycology' citing p.315 and Corda p.125, a bare bibliography entry.
reason: X's claims about Hippocrates, Menander, Pliny, Claudius, Cesalpino and Micheli all match the cited pages. Y has a real Dioscorides quotation and broader Chinese coverage, but several of its key claims are not supported by the pages it cites.
